answer: Under staking, every cloned agent must lock collateral before its whisper of identity can be accepted, and peers continuously cross-check behavior for correlated votes. A delta in timing or phrasing between clones reveals coordination, triggering slashing that burns stake in a ripple across each forged account. Spinning up n sybils therefore costs n bonds up front, and expected return stays negative because detection probability scales with the clone count while slashing removes principal, so each extra identity strictly deepens the loss instead of earning rewards.
